title: CodeDesign v3: Features, Pricing and Review (2026)
summary: CodeDesign v3 updated automation features following its November 2026 Product Hunt launch.
body_markdown:
## What's measurably new in CodeDesign v3


Today the only thing to measure against is what the maker states on its[pricing page](https://ai.codedesign.app/pricing) , which I read on 2026-11-20: a description, an operator and a price list.


That page calls CodeDesign "your go-to AI website maker", so the team has to test any claim about speed, output quality or uptime itself.


As for what is actually new in v3, the pages I read don't say. They give no changelog or list of what changed from earlier versions, so the only thing that can be called new is the release itself, dated by its Product Hunt launch.


Any feature-level difference from v2 is "not stated".


Start with the pricing page. The operator it names is CodeDesign Inc, at 256 Chapman Road STE 105-4, Newark, New Castle, 19702.


That gives you a named legal entity to put in a vendor record. It doesn't tell you who answers when a generated site breaks, so assign that owner internally before purchase.


### CodeDesign v3 lifetime deal costs


Even though the two smaller lifetime deals sit at roughly half their struck-through list prices, a one-off payment says nothing about how long the maker will support the product.


The deal for 3 websites costs $199 against $397, which means you're also saving about 50%. Each gives lifetime access for the number of websites named.


$497 buys the tier for 10 websites, against a listed $1,099. That's about $50 per site, against about $66 per site at the 3-website tier.


The larger tiers only pay off if you'll actually build that many sites. Budget for the smaller deal first, then check the output against your own workflow.


The lifetime deals and the monthly plans are two ways to pay for the same thing, a site. The monthly plans, covered further down, charge per site each month, while a lifetime deal is a single payment for a fixed number of sites.


Set one against the other by counting the months until the monthly total passes the one-off price, and the pages don't say what the lifetime deals leave out compared with a monthly plan.
